ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The lower end of the circuit in the figure is a common bottom node. The left branch is the voltage source Us, with the upper end marked “+” and the lower end marked “-”. Along the top from left to right are R1, the central node, R3, and the right-end node in sequence; R1 is marked with the reference direction of current I, with the arrow pointing to the right. The central node is connected downward through resistor R2 to the bottom common node. The right branch is the current source Is, with the arrow direction upward. Reasoning: Calculate the current in R1 in the arrow direction according to the superposition principle. 1) Keeping only Us and turning off Is, the current source is open-circuited, so there is no current in the R3 branch; Us only drives R1 and R2 in series, so I_U = 120/(3+12) = 8 A, with the direction consistent with the arrow. 2) Keeping only Is and turning off Us, the voltage source is short-circuited, and the left end of R1 is connected to the bottom node. The 5 A current source sends current through R3 into the central node, and the current at the central node divides between R1=3Ω and R2=12Ω in parallel. R1||R2 = 3*12/(3+12) = 12/5 = 2.4Ω, and the central node voltage V = 5*2.4 = 12 V. The magnitude of the R1 current is 12/3 = 4 A, and the direction is from the central node toward the left-end short-circuited node, that is, opposite to the arrow direction of I, so I_I = -4 A. Superposition gives I = I_U + I_I = 8 - 4 = 4.0 A.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit connections from the image, then compute two contributions. With Is turned off, the right branch is open, so R3 carries no current and Us drives series R1 and R2; the contribution through R1 in the arrow direction is I_U = 120/(3+12) = 8 A. With Us turned off, replace it by a short, so the left end of R1 is at the bottom node. The 5 A current source sends current through R3 into the central node, where it splits between R1=3 ohm and R2=12 ohm in parallel. The central node voltage is 5*(R1||R2)=5*(12/5)=12 V, so current in R1 is 12/3=4 A from the central node toward the shorted left node, opposite the indicated arrow; hence I_I = -4 A. Sum the superposed contributions: I = 8-4 = 4.0 A.

method.method_draft: First describe the node layout and current arrow from the image. For the Us-only case, open the current source, set V_A=120 V, and solve KCL at node B: (V_B-120)/3 + V_B/12 = 0. This gives V_B=96 V and I_U=(120-96)/3=8 A. For the Is-only case, short the voltage source so V_A=0. Use the upward current source as injecting 5 A into node C, so KCL at C gives (V_C-V_B)/3=5; KCL at B gives (V_B-0)/3 + V_B/12 + (V_B-V_C)/3 = 0. Solving gives V_B=12 V, so the R1 contribution in the indicated left-to-right direction is I_I=(0-12)/3=-4 A. Add contributions to obtain I=8+(-4)=4.0 A.

推理：用叠加原理。取底部公共节点为参考地。Us 单独作用时，电流源开路，VA = 120 V。节点 B 的 KCL 为 (VB - 120)/3 + VB/12 = 0，解得 VB = 96 V。因此 R1 中按图示左到右方向的电流贡献为 IU = (120 - 96)/3 = 8 A。Is 单独作用时，电压源短路，所以 VA = 0。向上的电流源向节点 C 注入 5 A，于是节点 C 的 KCL 可写为 (VC - VB)/3 = 5。节点 B 的 KCL 为 (VB - 0)/3 + VB/12 + (VB - VC)/3 = 0。联立可得 VB = 12 V。因此 R1 中按图示左到右方向的电流贡献为 II = (0 - 12)/3 = -4 A。叠加得到 I = 8 + (-4) = 4.0 A。
